answer: Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 39% independent neighbours on the funding graph. Because the walnut calculation reruns each epoch, the terrace weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the karst settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 91 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 38 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
